messages:
bot-incidents: ALERT: KV cache growth anomaly detected on us-west-2 serving cluster — rapid metadata expansion + batch latency spike. severity: P1. auto-runbooks triggered. link: https://internal/incident/2009876543 :rotating_light:

maria (eng-runtime): saw it pop up in dashboards; KV metadata count jumped ~7x in 4m. continuous-batch latency jumped from 50ms -> 750ms on some backends.

sanjay (oncall): I'm on it. collecting traces now. initial customer impact: increased tail latency for hosted API, some 504s.

Elaine (SRE): any obvious recent rollout? storage config change?

Jordan (infra): no infra deploys in last hour. I do see GC pressure on block-manager host group bm-west-2-a.

maria (eng-runtime): suspect paged KV block metadata leak + continuous batching magnifying it. we've seen similar pattern in canary months ago.

bot-incidents: Automated triage: top processes: block-manager(oom_retry=3), runtime-worker. Suggested mitigation steps: 1) reduce continuous-batch window to 10ms 2) cap KV prefetched blocks per model to 128 3) enable safer-eviction-policy=aggressive-temp

Priya (eng-ml): reduce batch window now? that will increase request count but should reduce per-batch token blowout.

maria (eng-runtime): I can push a runtime config change to reduce batch window and throttle prefetch caps. patch ready. needs manual approval for production.

Ryan (support): PS: Customer AlphaCorp reported degraded interactive response times ~10:12. They pasted logs showing repeated "block-meta-miss" and 504s.

Alex (customer-success): I'm on a zoom with AlphaCorp CS and will update after mitigation. they're seeing consumer-facing slowness, impact level: medium-high.

maria (eng-runtime): Pushing hotfix: set continuous_batch.max_window_ms=10 and kv.prefetch.max_blocks=128 to canary subset (10%) now. rolling update to 20% if green.

TriageBot: Action logged by sanjay. Playbook step: "apply hotfix -> observe 5m".

sanjay (oncall): approving canary. maria, run the canary. ping @Elaine for rollout approval if canary stable.

maria (eng-runtime): canary applied to cluster bm-west-2-a subset-3 at 2009876610.

Jordan (infra): I'm throttling new prefetched block allocations at the host-level for bm-west-2-a to reduce churn. command run on host group: `hostctl set kv_prefetch_limit 128`

Elaine (SRE): watching CPU/mem and request error rate. setting alert: if 5xx rate > 2% for 3m -> rollback.

maria (eng-runtime): early telemetry looks promising: metadata growth rate dropped by ~60% in canary nodes, P50 latency back to 70ms but P99 still elevated.

Priya (eng-ml): curious if quantized model variant has different cache behavior — could route a small portion to it as fallback.

maria (eng-runtime): not yet. prefer to stabilize runtime first. but can prepare fallback model variant if needed.

Ryan (support): AlphaCorp reports partial improvement at 10:22 — some requests faster but intermittently still slow.

Alex (customer-success): telling AlphaCorp we're doing targeted mitigations, will follow up with postmortem. they asked for ETA; will say 30-60min for stabilization.

maria (eng-runtime): stepping canary to 50% at 2009876725. no errors except one node with repeated block-manager thrash; isolating it from rotation.

Jordan (infra): isolated node bm-west-2-a-7; restarting block-manager process there to clear stale metadata. command: `systemctl restart block-manager`

TriageBot: Incident timeline note appended: canary -> 50% -> node isolate and restart.

Elaine (SRE): after the restart isolated node drops to stable mem footprint. overall 5xx rate decreased to 0.8% cluster-wide.

maria (eng-runtime): rolling to 100% with same config at 2009876810. keeping prefetch cap and aggressive-temp eviction until stable for 45m.

Priya (eng-ml): would recommend a post-incident eval to run a prompt suite and check response divergence after batch-window change — batching affects output ordering & latency-sensitive heuristics.

sanjay (oncall): agreed. we'll schedule an eval run. @maria please include flags and kernel versions used during the hotfix.

Ryan (support): AlphaCorp confirms much improved performance at 10:35, they're able to proceed. will close escalation once we confirm 1h stability.

Alex (customer-success): conveyed to AlphaCorp. they're appreciative of the fast response. recorded ticket #CS-1298.

maria (eng-runtime): post-rollback plan: keep limits for 24h, then test incremental raise of prefetch cap with traffic shadow and verify metadata delta. also investigate root cause: block metadata accumulation path — likely a race in eviction when metadata invalidation overlaps with async prefetch completion.

Jordan (infra): filing infra follow-up: host-level guardrails for prefetched blocks and metrics to track per-model block allocations over time.

Priya (eng-ml): I'll run a repro harness with heavy continuous-batch traces to try and reproduce the metadata leak locally.

Elaine (SRE): longer-term action items documented. assigning owners: maria (runtime fix + postmortem), Jordan (infra guardrails), Priya (repro + test harness), Ryan/Alex (customer comms).

sanjay (oncall): handing off to day oncall loop. I'll leave a monitoring playbook in the incident doc. final status: mitigation successful, customer impact reduced to low.

bot-incidents: Incident P1 -> transitioned to monitoring. Postmortem requested. See https://internal/incident/2009876543/postmortem

maria (eng-runtime): quick note — we applied an aggressive eviction heuristic that increases eviction score for blocks with repeated meta-miss. need to evaluate false positives. adding to postmortem.

Ryan (support): closing the active customer escalation thread, will reopen if AlphaCorp reports regression.

Alex (customer-success): scheduling customer follow-up tomorrow, sending summary and action items.

TriageBot: Incident thread archived at 2009876930. Thanks team :heart:
